candidates.attacker_control: The `from` query parameter of `/loginEntry` (e.g. `/loginEntry?from=//evil.example`), fully attacker-controlled and deliverable as a link/redirect to a victim.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The endpoint only redirects after container authentication (`getUserPrincipal() != null`), so it is not an unauthenticated trigger; the Javadoc says doLoginEntry is used only by LegacySecurityRealm (deprecated), limiting real-world exposure; the `//host` browser behavior was not runtime-tested and container handling of scheme-relative Location values was not verified; no CVE/patch lookup was performed (not permitted), so it is unconfirmed whether a later upstream fix targets this line.
candidates.impact: Open redirect/phishing from the Jenkins origin; can be chained with credential-harvesting or trusted-origin OAuth/SSO redirect flows. Requires user interaction and (in current code) is primarily on the legacy login-entry path, so severity is limited.
candidates.prerequisites: Victim must be logged in so that `req.getUserPrincipal() != null`; the path is subject to the root READ check, which most authenticated (and often anonymous) users have; the method is documented as being used by the deprecated LegacySecurityRealm but the URL binding exists on Jenkins for all realms; victim must follow the crafted link.
candidates.root_cause: The `from` request parameter is validated only with `from.startsWith("/")` before being passed to `rsp.sendRedirect2(from)`. Scheme-relative URLs such as `//evil.example` satisfy that prefix test and are emitted in the Location header as `//evil.example`, which browsers resolve to `https://evil.example`. The rest of the codebase uses `Util.isSafeToRedirectTo` (rejects absolute and scheme-relative URLs) for exactly this purpose (e.g. AuthenticationSuccessHandler, ParametersDefinitionProperty, DirectoryBrowserSupport, ManageJenkinsAction), so this site is an inconsistent outlier.
candidates.title: Open redirect in Jenkins.doLoginEntry via `from=//host` (startsWith("/") guard bypass instead of Util.isSafeToRedirectTo)
candidates.trace: GET /loginEntry?from=//evil.example -> doLoginEntry: from = "//evil.example"; `from.startsWith("/")` is true and `!from.equals("/loginError")` is true -> rsp.sendRedirect2("//evil.example") -> servlet container writes `Location: //evil.example` -> the browser interprets this as a scheme-relative URL and navigates to the attacker-controlled host, from an origin the user trusts (no Util.isSafeToRedirectTo check).
candidates.unverified: Whether Jenkins' container (Jetty/Winstone) preserves `//host` verbatim in Location in all deployments; whether instances using modern realms ever dispatch /loginEntry in practice; whether this corresponds to any known CVE/fix; no execution or runtime confirmation.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

coverage_summary: Scope: get_source_scope reports 9,959 visible files (binary-like files refused; 5 MiB per-file limit; 0 excluded by name/symlink). get_relation_scope reports a partial syntactic index over 9,907 files (1,196 Java files; 18 parsed units reported; 52 source files missing from the index; 28,802 unresolved calls), with no control-flow, no data-flow, no semantic resolution and unverified Spring annotations - so index facts were used only for navigation and every cited edge was verified in source text. I reviewed core security packages (hudson.security.*, jenkins.security.* including csrf/apitoken/stapler/seed), the CLI module and CLI commands, ACL/permission model and MANAGE/SYSTEM_READ rollout, plugin manager/update center, FilePath/DirectoryBrowserSupport path handling, console notes, Secret/XStream2 configuration, resource-domain tokens, and administrative monitors, plus grep sweeps for command execution, deserialization, XML parsers, redirects, cookie flags, weak randomness and permission/POST enforcement. Not reviewed: the majority of the ~1,196 Java files and all JS/webapp resources in depth, and runtime behavior. Snapshot contains no test sources, no Jelly views and no binary CA/plugin artifacts (files are documented as omitted/refused), so view-rendering and test-based verification were impossible.
limitations: No runtime execution, build, or dependency verification was performed (not permitted); all conclusions are static.
The relation index is partial and syntactic only (no data/control flow), and 52 source files are absent from it; absence of an index record is not evidence of absence of code.
The snapshot excludes tests, Jelly views and binary files (e.g. update-center CA certificates), so UI-layer escaping, view wiring and certificate material could not be inspected.
No patch/CVE/advisory lookup was allowed, so I could not map the snapshot to a known fixed vulnerability; the submitted candidate is a source-level lead, not a confirmed bug.
The open-redirect candidate depends on container/browser handling of scheme-relative Location values and on dispatch of /loginEntry outside the legacy realm, neither of which was runtime-confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: hudson.util.Secret.decrypt missing payload-length validation: isValidData accepts `{AQ==}`; Base64 decode yields a 1-byte array so the PAYLOAD_V1 branch reads payload[1..8] and throws an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (reachable via Secret.fromString, Stapler CONVERT_UTILS String conversion, Secret.ConverterImpl.unmarshal, and ExtendedReadSecretRedaction).
rejected_leads.reason: Provable crash path, but impact is availability/500 only and most practical triggers require a user who can already submit form/config data (self-DoS); not the strongest security-impact candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: ACL.hasCreatePermission2 returning `true` when the deprecated hasCreatePermission is not overridden (fail-open authorization).
rejected_leads.reason: Appears to be intentional upstream design: callers (ItemGroupMixIn create/copy, View.create) separately check Item.CREATE/View.CREATE, so the method only adds optional per-descriptor granularity; no exploitable path found in core.

rejected_leads.lead: AdministrativeMonitor doAct implementations that mutate state without an explicit ADMINISTER check (BuiltInNodeMigration, ApiTokenPropertyDisabledDefault/EnabledNewLegacy, SecurityIsOffMonitor, ControllerExecutors*, HudsonHomeDiskUsageMonitor, PluginWrapperAdministrativeMonitor).
rejected_leads.reason: All are gated by AdministrativeMonitor.getTarget() -> checkRequiredPermission(), which defaults to Jenkins.ADMINISTER when getRequiredPermission() is not overridden; monitors that do expose themselves to SYSTEM_READ (ReverseProxySetupMonitor, TooManyJobsButNoView, JavaVersionRecommendation, OperatingSystemEndOfLife, ResourceDomainRecommendation, UpdateSiteWarningsMonitor) do perform explicit ADMINISTER checks. No bypass found.

rejected_leads.lead: ExtendedReadSecretRedaction/ExtendedReadRedaction masking might be bypassable (secret disclosure to Item.EXTENDED_READ/SystemRead users).
rejected_leads.reason: The redaction is wired into AbstractItem.writeConfigDotXml, Computer.doConfigDotXml, View.doConfigDotXmlImpl, ItemGroupMixIn.copy and GetJob/GetNode/GetView CLI commands; the regex matches realistic XStream output and Secret.decrypt filters false positives. No reproducible masking gap found; not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: ReverseProxySetupMonitor.getTestForReverseProxySetup(String rest) reflects the user-controlled URL remainder into an error message (potential reflected XSS for SYSTEM_READ users).
rejected_leads.reason: Could not establish that the container/HttpResponses.errorWithoutStack renders the message as unescaped HTML; all other errorWithoutStack messages in core are plain text, and the endpoint is SYSTEM_READ-gated. Unverified.

rejected_leads.lead: Other redirect/authorization sinks checked and found guarded: DirectoryBrowserSupport pattern/path redirect, ParametersDefinitionProperty redirectTo, AuthenticationSuccessHandler, BuildAuthorizationToken, Computer.doConfigDotXml/updateByXml, UpdateCenter doUpgrade/doRestart, PluginManager install/upload, CLI node lifecycle commands (cliConnect/cliDisconnect/cliOffline), Queue.doCancelItem, User token endpoints.
rejected_leads.reason: Each has an appropriate permission check and/or POST requirement; the CLI @-syntax file-read class (CVE-2024-23897-style) is fixed in this snapshot.

summary: Reviewed the assigned Jenkins core snapshot (revision 2.504-SNAPSHOT, ~2025-03-25) as a defensive source review. I focused on trust boundaries and attacker-controlled input: HTTP/CLI entry points, authorization (ACL/Item/Computer/Jenkins permissions, the new MANAGE/SYSTEM_READ model), CSRF (CrumbFilter/CrumbIssuers/POST enforcement), secret handling (`Secret`, `ExtendedReadRedaction`, config.xml exposures), path handling (`DirectoryBrowserSupport`, `FilePath`), agent/JNLP and resource-domain token handling, deserialization (XStream/JEP-200, console notes), and redirect handling. The well-known CLI `@`-file-read class is fixed in this snapshot (`CLICommand.ALLOW_AT_SYNTAX` defaults to false and is enforced in `CmdLineParser`/`CLIRegisterer`), and the recent secret-redaction framework (SECURITY-266 follow-up) is fully wired into AbstractItem/Computer/View and the CLI readers. No high-confidence vulnerability was confirmed. The single strongest lead I can defend from source is a remaining open-redirect sink in `Jenkins.doLoginEntry` that ignores the codebase's own `Util.isSafeToRedirectTo` guard; it is a lead, not a confirmed exploit, and several other suspicious spots were checked and rejected with reasons below.
